report.interpretation: I read "outlier on cost" as average incurred cost (paid plus reserve) per auto claim handled by each repair shop. Only collision, glass and hail claims have a shop. To keep the comparison fair, I compared each claim with the average for the same cause and state, then averaged those ratios per shop (a cost index, where 1.0 is typical). I excluded the 159 duplicated payment rows from the 2026-03-14 reload batch. The period is all loss dates, 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-30.
report.answer: Yes, one shop stands out: RS-041 Campbell Body Works (IL, non-preferred). It has 79 claims at an average incurred cost of about $5,774. That is a cost index of 1.38, meaning 38% above what the same causes and states cost elsewhere, and about 3.5 standard deviations above the typical shop. Other shops average $4,198 per claim, and other Illinois shops average $3,499. The next highest shops are RS-029 Thomas Auto Repair (NC) at 1.20 and RS-024 Johnston Body Works (GA) at 1.16. Both are within normal spread. They are small samples (23 and 42 claims) and not clear outliers. This is a statistical flag, not proof of overcharging. It's worth a review of the shop's invoices.
report.answer_sql: with p as (select claim_id, sum(amount) paid from claim_payments where load_batch not like 'reload-%' group by 1), c as (select c.*, coalesce(p.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount inc from claims c left join p using(claim_id) where repair_shop_id is not null), e as (select cause, state, avg(inc) exp_inc from c group by all) select c.repair_shop_id, r.name, count(*) n, round(avg(inc)) avg_incurred, round(avg(inc/e.exp_inc),2) cost_index from c join e using(cause,state) join repair_shops r using(repair_shop_id) group by all order by cost_index desc limit 1

findings.claim: RS-041 Campbell Body Works (IL, non-preferred) is a clear cost outlier after adjusting for cause and state.
findings.evidence_sql: with p as (select claim_id, sum(amount) paid from claim_payments where load_batch not like 'reload-%' group by 1), c as (select c.*, coalesce(p.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount inc from claims c left join p using(claim_id) where repair_shop_id is not null), e as (select cause, state, avg(inc) exp_inc from c group by all) select c.repair_shop_id, count(*) n, round(avg(inc)) avg_incurred, round(avg(inc/e.exp_inc),2) cost_index from c join e using(cause,state) group by 1 order by 4 desc limit 5

key_numbers.label: Cost index vs same cause and state

data_quality_issues.issue: 159 payment rows were loaded twice, in batch reload-2026-03-14 (payments dated 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13).
data_quality_issues.impact: I excluded them. Left in, they would inflate paid amounts for the affected claims and could distort shop averages.

data_quality_issues.issue: Recent claims are incomplete because of late reporting, and open claims carry estimated reserves.
data_quality_issues.impact: Incurred amounts for recent claims may still change. This affects all shops, so the ranking should hold up.

data_quality_issues.issue: 322 payment amounts are unusually large (the largest is $237,119).
data_quality_issues.impact: Large payments can pull a shop's average up. I didn't remove them, and RS-041's median is also high ($4,366 against roughly $3,300 to $4,000 for most other shops).

proposed_actions.title: Review RS-041 Campbell Body Works invoices and estimates
proposed_actions.reason: Its average claim cost is 38% above peers for the same cause and state. Check for inflated estimates, supplementary charges or a cluster of large claims.

open_questions: Did you mean cost per claim? I can also compare shops on repair cycle time, or compare preferred and non-preferred shops.
